function: Joint active (BS transmit beamforming) and passive (coupled phase-shift STAR-RIS) beamforming by a SAC deep reinforcement learning agent to maximize the long-term sum secrecy rate (pp. 1-3).
system: Downlink MIMO: BS with N=4 antennas, passive lossless coupled phase-shift STAR-RIS (energy splitting) with M=8 elements, two 4-antenna users, two 2-antenna eavesdroppers; band not stated (pp. 2, 4).
method: Soft actor-critic reinforcement learning: one policy network and two soft Q-networks with targets; state is the channel CSI, action the beamforming coefficients; replay buffer (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulator: BS-to-STAR-RIS link Rician, other links Rayleigh, with distance path loss, Rician factor 5 dB; no standardized, measured or public channel data (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Training and evaluation in the same simulated environment (30 s process); results swept over reflection elements M=4-20 and BS antennas N=4, 8; no test in unseen conditions (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Random STAR-RIS phase shifts, double spliced conventional RIS, independent-phase STAR-RIS (designs not described); DDPG of [13] named in text, not plotted in Fig. 4 (pp. 4-5).
metrics: Sum secrecy rate (bps/Hz) versus reflection elements; episode reward (cumulative sum secrecy rate) versus training episodes for learning rates and BS antennas (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "The channel matrix G is modeled as the Rician fading channel" (custom Rician/Rayleigh model with path loss, p. 4; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is mentioned).
q2_support: p. 5: "Fig. 5 shows the reward convergence of the three schemes" (training curves for BS antennas N=4 and N=8; no trained agent is tested in a scenario not used for training).
q3_support: p. 5: "performs better than the DDPG algorithm" (DDPG scheme of [13] is the earlier learned baseline); p. 5: "the random phase-shift scheme" (non-learned baseline). The Fig. 4 legend plots no DDPG curve, so the mark rests on the text.
q4_support: p. 4: "The SAC algorithm training parameters are shown in Table I." (Table I lists only training hyperparameters; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime is reported).
q5_support: p. 4: "Two users and two eavesdroppers are located on each side of the STAR-RIS" (own simulated geometry and channel; no link to code or data, no public dataset).
notes: Published IEEE Communications Letters version. Secrecy-rate beamforming with a STAR-RIS is area 3 (it is not authentication or anti-jamming). The text names a DDPG scheme [13] among the four compared schemes, yet Figs. 4 and 5 plot only independent-phase, coupled-phase, double spliced and random-phase curves; q3 rests on the text statement and the reviewer should confirm. The Fig. 4 axis is labelled N but the caption and text say M. CSI is computed with a factor graph algorithm [15] (p. 2).
